<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_section"><a href="#S4" title="In Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref">IV </span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">The proposed E-JSG</span></span></a>
<ol class="ltx_toclist ltx_toclist_section">
<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_subsection"><a href="#S4.SS1" title="In IV The proposed E-JSG ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref"><span class="ltx_text">IV-A</span> </span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The Proposed E-JSG</span></span></a>
<ol class="ltx_toclist ltx_toclist_subsection">
<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_subsubsection"><a href="#S4.SS1.SSS1" title="In IV-A The Proposed E-JSG ‣ IV The proposed E-JSG ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref"><span class="ltx_text">IV-A</span>1 </span>Linear encoding-inspired VI graph design</span></a></li>
<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_subsubsection"><a href="#S4.SS1.SSS2" title="In IV-A The Proposed E-JSG ‣ IV The proposed E-JSG ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref"><span class="ltx_text">IV-A</span>2 </span>Update of BVNs to CNs and FNs</span></a></li>
<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_subsubsection"><a href="#S4.SS1.SSS3" title="In IV-A The Proposed E-JSG ‣ IV The proposed E-JSG ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref"><span class="ltx_text">IV-A</span>3 </span>Update of CNs and FNs to BVNs</span></a></li>
</ol></li>

</ol></li>
</ol></nav>
</nav>

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document"> Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design </h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Qu Luo
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Jing Zhu
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Zilong Liu
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Yanqun Tang
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Pei Xiao
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Gaojie Chen
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Jia Shi
</span><span id="id1" class="ltx_note ltx_note_frontmatter ltx_thanks_note ltx_role_thanks"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_type">thanks: </span><span id="id1.1" class="ltx_text">
Qu Luo, Jing Zhu, Pei Xiao and Gaojie Chen are with the 5G &amp; 6G Innovation Centre, University of Surrey, U. K. (email: {q.u.luo, j.zhu, p.xiao, gaojie.chen }@surrey.ac.uk).
Zilong Liu is with the School of Computer Science and Electronics Engineering, University of Essex, U. K. (email:  zilong.liu@essex.ac.uk).
Yanqun Tang is with the School of Electronics and Communication Engineering, Sun Yat-sen University, China (email: tangyq8@mail.sysu.edu.cn).
Jia Shi is with the School of Telecommunications Engineering, Xidian University, Xi’an, China (email: jiashi@xidian.edu.cn). </span></span></span></span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_text">Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) is a promising chirp-assisted multicarrier waveform for future high-mobility communications. This paper is devoted to enhanced receiver design for multiple-input–multiple-output AFDM (MIMO-AFDM) systems. Firstly, we introduce a unified variational inference (VI) approach to approximate the target posterior distribution, under which the belief propagation (BP) and expectation propagation (EP)-based algorithms are derived. As both VI-based detection and low-density parity-check (LDPC) decoding can be expressed by bipartite graphs in MIMO-AFDM systems, we construct a joint sparse graph (JSG) by merging the graphs of these two for low-complexity receiver design. Then, based on this graph model, we present the detailed message propagation of the proposed JSG. Additionally, we propose an enhanced JSG (E-JSG) receiver based on the linear constellation encoding model. The proposed E-JSG eliminates the need for interleavers, de-interleavers, and log-likelihood ratio transformations, thus leading to concurrent detection and decoding  over the integrated sparse graph. To further reduce detection complexity, we introduce a sparse channel method by approaximating multiple graph edges with insignificant channel coefficients into a single edge on the VI graph. Simulation results show the superiority of the proposed receivers in terms of computational complexity, detection and decoding latency, and error rate performance compared to the conventional ones.</span></p>
  
</div>
<div class="ltx_keywords">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_keywords">Index Terms: </h6><span id="id2" class="ltx_text">Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM), multiple-input–multiple-output AFDM (MIMO-AFDM), variational inference (VI), joint sparse graph, low complexity detection and decoding.
</span>
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">I </span><span id="S1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Introduction</span></h2>

<section id="S1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S1.SS1.6" class="ltx_text">I-A</span> </span><span id="S1.SS1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Background</span></h3>

<div id="S1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Next generation wireless systems and standards e.g., beyond 5G, 6G are envisioned to provide a wide range of data services, including ultra-reliable, high-rate, and low-latency communications in  highly dynamic environments, such as vehicle-to-everything, unmanned aerial vehicles, high-speed trains, and low-earth-orbit satellite systems, etc. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">Toward</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">9779322</span>]</cite>. In these scenarios, one often needs to deal with the rapidly time-varying channels <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">otfsHIGH</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">zhou2023overview</span>]</cite>.
The legacy multicarrier systems primarily rely on orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), thanks to its advantages (e.g., efficient hardware implementation, capability of intersymbol interference mitigation) in linear time-invariant channels <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">BroadbandOFDM</span>]</cite>. Nevertheless, OFDM is sensitive to carrier frequency offsets and Doppler shifts/spreads in rapidly time-varying channels and hence may suffer from drastically degraded error performances <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">otfsHIGH</span>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Extensive efforts have been dedicated to designing novel modulation waveforms to support reliable communications in high mobility channels. For example, orthogonal time–frequency space (OTFS) modulation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">otfsHIGH</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">RavitejaOTFS</span>]</cite> and orthogonal chirp division multiplexing (OCDM) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">OrthogonalcdmOuyang</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">OCDMPerformance</span>]</cite> have attracted substantial research attention. The former modulates the information symbols in the delay-Doppler domain instead of the conventional time–frequency domain. By doing so, one can effectively convert a time-variant channel into a two-dimensional (2D) quasi-static channel in delay-Doppler domain <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">otfsHIGH</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">YuanOTFS1</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">RavitejaOTFS</span>]</cite>.
In contrast, OCDM, building upon the discrete Fresnel transform (DFnT), modulates the information symbols using a class of orthogonal chirp subcarriers (SCs) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">OrthogonalcdmOuyang</span>]</cite>.
Both OTFS and OCDM have demonstrated superior error performances over OFDM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">Haifocdm</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">AFDMTWCBemani</span>]</cite>.
However, the 2D structure of OTFS requires radical change of the transceivers (compared to that of OFDM), whilst it suffers from large overhead for sending pilots and multiuser signals <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">AFDMTWCBemani</span>]</cite>. OCDM, on the other hand, may not be able to achieve optimal performance when its chirp rate does not fit the specific delay-Doppler profile of the channel <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">AFDMTWCBemani</span>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Recently, Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) is another appealing solution for efficient and reliable communications over high-mobility channels <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">AFDMTWCBemani</span>]</cite>. Similar to OCDM, information symbols in AFDM are multiplexed on a number of orthogonal chirp SCs through the discrete
affine Fourier transform (DAFT) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">ErsegheAFDM</span>]</cite>. By appropriately adjusting the chirp rate based on the delay-Doppler profile of the channel, AFDM enables a separable and quasi-static channel representation, thereby achieving full diversity over doubly selective channels <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">AFDMTWCBemani</span>]</cite>. Since the DAFT employed in AFDM is a generalization of many other transforms, such as the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) and DFnT, AFDM generalizes OFDM and OCDM as special cases.
More importantly, AFDM enjoys a high compatibility to the legacy OFDM as DAFT can be efficiently implemented through fast Fourier transform (FFT) with additional two one-tap filters <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">BemaniAFDM_conf1</span>]</cite>. These advantages make AFDM as a promising candidate multicarrier waveform for the next generation
wireless systems <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">NiAFDMSens</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">savaux2023dft</span>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S1.SS2.6" class="ltx_text">I-B</span> </span><span id="S1.SS2.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Related Works</span></h3>

<div id="S1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">AFDM has attracted a plethora of research attempts from various aspects, such as system impairments <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">BemaniAFDM_conf1</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">tang2023time</span>]</cite>, channel estimation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">YinChannel</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">yin2022channel</span>]</cite>, signal detection <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">bemani2022low</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">wu2023message</span>]</cite>, and intergrated sensing and communications <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">zhu2023low</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">ni2022afdm</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">IntegratedAFDM</span>]</cite>.
The authors in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">BemaniAFDM_conf1</span>]</cite> evaluated the performance of AFDM over high-mobility scenarios and in high-frequency bands. It is shown that AFDM is robust to the impairments such as carrier frequency offset and phase noise. The time and frequency offset estimations for AFDM synchronization
have been studied in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">tang2023time</span>]</cite>.
In <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">YinChannel</span>]</cite>, both single pilot and multiple pilots aided channel estimation schemes for AFDM were considered. In <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">yin2022channel</span>]</cite>, an embedded pilot-aided channel estimation scheme for AFDM with multiple input and multiple output (MIMO), called MIMO-AFDM, was investigated. Moreover, a low complexity iterative decision feedback equalizer based on weighted maximal ratio combining scheme was introduced in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">bemani2022low</span>]</cite> for efficient symbol detection by exploiting the channel sparsity in AFDM. A generalized message passing algorithm (MPA)-based detection scheme was developed in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">wu2023message</span>]</cite>. However, the complexity of the MPA detector grows exponentially as the number of multipaths increases. By fully exploiting its  inherent chirp nature of AFDM, it has also been applied for integrated sensing and communications (ISAC). In particular, a low complexity algorithm based on matched filtering was developed in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">zhu2023low</span>]</cite> for estimating high resolution target range with the AFDM waveform. In <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">ni2022afdm</span>]</cite>, an AFDM-based ISAC system was introduced, which utilizes a time-domain parameter estimation scheme. Very recently, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">IntegratedAFDM</span>]</cite> proposed an AFDM-based ISAC system using only chirp subcarrier. It shows that sensing with one chirp subcarrier allows simple self-interference cancellation,
thus avoiding the need for expensive full duplex methods.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">AFDM has also been integrated with code-domain non-orthogonal multiple access or modulation to achieve higher spectrum efficiency and enhanced reliability <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">luo2023afdm</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">tao2023affine</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">zhu2023design</span>]</cite>. Specifically, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">luo2023afdm</span>]</cite> and <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">10683521</span>]</cite> studied the AFDM-empowered sparse code multiple access (SCMA) for massive connectivity over high mobility communications. In comparison to OFDM-SCMA, AFDM-SCMA exhibits significantly improved error performance. In addition, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">tao2023affine</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">zhu2023design</span>]</cite> proposed index modulation (IM)-empowered AFDM systems, which was shown to outperform its OFDM-IM counterpart.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S1.SS3.6" class="ltx_text">I-C</span> </span><span id="S1.SS3.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Motivations and Contributions</span></h3>

<div id="S1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The aforementioned works have shown the advantages of AFDM in high-mobility communications due to its ability to achieve <span id="S1.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">full diversity</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">AFDMTWCBemani</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">BemaniAFDM_conf1</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">luo2023afdm</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">tao2023affine</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">zhu2023design</span>]</cite>. However, the <span id="S1.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">full diversity</span> can only be attained with a sophisticated receiver that implements the optimal maximum <span id="S1.SS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">a posteriori</span> (MAP) detection <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">MaximumdIVERSITY</span>]</cite>, such as MPA and sphere decoder. In addition, it should be noted that existing works on AFDM generally focused on uncoded systems and little has  been reported on the coded AFDM system performances. Recently, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">OCDMPerformance</span>]</cite> compared the uncoded and coded BER performances of OCDM and OFDM by employing a minimum mean square error (MMSE) detector and a rate-<math id="S1.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/3</annotation></semantics></math> convolutional code. It was shown in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">OCDMPerformance</span>]</cite> that OCDM achieves better uncoded BER performance but similar coded BER performance compared to OFDM. This is reasonable due to the frequency diversity attained by coded OFDM. The above observations can be readily extended to AFDM systems due to its generic chirp nature.
This also implies that enhanced  detection and decoding in AFDM should be carefully designed by considering its inherent features for fully exploiting the diversity gain. In addition, while there is extensive literature on efficient iterative receiver design, such as the Turbo iterative structure <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">EnhancingLUo</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">hanzo2007turbo</span>]</cite> and orthogonal approximate message passing design <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">liu2024capacity</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">luo2023afdm</span>]</cite>, developing more advanced and low-complexity AFDM receiver remains largely unexplored.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">On the other hand, the amalgamation of MIMO and AFDM, i.e., MIMO-AFDM, can be leveraged to achieve higher spectrum efficiency and lower error rate. Although the channel estimation of MIMO-AFDM was studied in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">YinChannel</span>]</cite>, the efficient receiver design in MIMO-AFDM is a largely open research topic.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Against the above background and research gaps, this paper aims to develop novel low-complexity joint detection and decoding schemes fully exploiting the system diversity in MIMO-AFDM systems. Specifically, we formulate the MIMO-AFDM detection as a Bayesian inference problem for computing the marginal posterior distribution <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">Zhaoofts</span>]</cite>.  We advocate the use of variational inference (VI) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">Advancesvi</span>]</cite> as an approximate inference algorithm in probabilistic models. The principle of VI is to approximate the target posterior distribution using a simple distribution, thereby transforming an intractable inference problem into a tractable one <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">VIchen</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">WeijieVI</span>]</cite>. Our second key innovation is to represent the joint distribution of the transmitted and received signal in MIMO-AFDM as a sparse factor graph, referred to as the VI graph. By adopting low-density parity check (LDPC) codes as the channel code <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">WenJSG</span>]</cite>, we merge the VI graph and the relevant LDPC factor graph into a joint sparse graph
(JSG).</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The main contributions of this paper are summarized as follows:</p>
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We formulate MIMO-AFDM detection as a Bayesian inference problem for computing the marginal posterior distribution. Specifically, we introduce a unified VI approach to approximate the target posterior distribution, upon which the belief propagation (BP) and expectation propagation (EP)-based algorithms can be derived.
Subsequently, both BP-JSG and EP-JSG are employed for highly efficient message propagation.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Inspired by the linear constellation encoding model, we introduce an enhanced JSG (E-JSG) to eliminate the use of interleavers, de-interleavers, symbol-to-bit, and bit-to-symbol log-likelihood ratio (LLR) transformations. As such, one can merge the detection and decoding for E-JSG by efficiently passing the belief messages over the integrated sparse graph. In addition, for reduced receiver processing, we propose a sparse channel method. The main idea of this approach is to approximate multiple graph edges with insignificant channel coefficients into a single edge on the VI graph.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We present extensive numerical results to demonstrate the superiority of the proposed JSG receivers in terms of lower computational complexity and reduced detection and decoding latency compared to conventional MMSE and turbo-like receivers. Furthermore, the proposed JSG receivers can exploit multipath diversity and Doppler diversity in MIMO-AFDM systems more efficiently, giving rise to improved coded BER performance compared to conventional receivers.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S1.SS4.6" class="ltx_text">I-D</span> </span><span id="S1.SS4.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Organization</span></h3>

<div id="S1.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This paper is organized as follows: Section <a href="#S2" title="II MIMO-AFDM Communication Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">II</span></a> describes the system model of MIMO-AFDM. The proposed VI-JSG is presented in Section <a href="#S3" title="III Variational Inference and Graphical Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">III</span></a>, covering the principles of VI, joint factor representation of MIMO-AFDM, and the message passing in VI-JSG. Section <a href="#S4" title="IV The proposed E-JSG ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">IV</span></a> introduces the proposed enhanced VI-JSG and the complexity reduction in the JSG. The simulation results are presented and discussed
in Section <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_label ltx_ref_self"></span>. Section <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_label ltx_ref_self"></span> concludes the paper.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S1.SS5.6" class="ltx_text">I-E</span> </span><span id="S1.SS5.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Notation</span></h3>

<div id="S1.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The <math id="S1.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional complex, real and binary vector spaces are denoted as <math id="S1.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{C}^{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℂ</mi><mi>n</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{C}^{n}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S1.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>n</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{n}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.SS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{B}^{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝔹</mi><mi>n</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{B}^{n}</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively. Similarly, <math id="S1.SS5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{C}^{k\times n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℂ</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{C}^{k\times n}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S1.SS5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{k\times n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{k\times n}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.SS5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{B}^{k\times n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝔹</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{B}^{k\times n}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the <math id="S1.SS5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(k\times n)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(k\times n)</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional complex, real and binary matrix spaces, respectively.
<math id="S1.SS5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{CN}(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{CN}(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the
complex Gaussian distribution with zero-mean and unit-variance. <math id="S1.SS5.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{{\mathbf{I}}_{n}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐈</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{{\mathbf{I}}_{n}}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes an <math id="S1.SS5.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\times n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\times n</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional identity matrix. <math id="S1.SS5.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{diag}(\mathbf{x})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>diag</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{diag}(\mathbf{x})</annotation></semantics></math> gives a diagonal matrix with the diagonal vector of <math id="S1.SS5.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math>. <math id="S1.SS5.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\cdot)^{\mathcal{T}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\cdot)^{\mathcal{T}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.SS5.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\cdot)^{\mathcal{H}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\cdot)^{\mathcal{H}}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the transpose and the Hermitian transpose operation, respectively.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">II </span><span id="S2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MIMO-AFDM Communication Model</span></h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section introduces the MIMO-AFDM signal model. Specifically, we start by introducing the AFDM modulation, channel, demodulation and input-output (I/O) relation in the single-input and single-output AFDM (SISO-AFDM) system, which is shown in Fig. <a href="#S2.F1" title="Fig. 1 ‣ II-A1 AFDM modulation ‣ II-A SISO-AFDM Communication Model ‣ II MIMO-AFDM Communication Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. Subsequently, we extend the SISO-AFDM to the MIMO-AFDM case.</p>
</div>
<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S2.SS1.6" class="ltx_text">II-A</span> </span><span id="S2.SS1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">SISO-AFDM Communication Model</span></h3>

<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section presents the signal model of a SISO-AFDM system, as shown in Fig. <a href="#S2.F1" title="Fig. 1 ‣ II-A1 AFDM modulation ‣ II-A SISO-AFDM Communication Model ‣ II MIMO-AFDM Communication Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection"><span id="S2.SS1.SSS1.6" class="ltx_text">II-A</span>1 </span>AFDM modulation</h4>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Denoted  <math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{\text{SISO}}\in\mathbb{C}^{N\times 1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mtext>SISO</mtext></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℂ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{\text{SISO}}\in\mathbb{C}^{N\times 1}</annotation></semantics></math> by the transmitted vector in the DAFT domain. Then the modulated symbol is obtained by taking the IDAFT of  <math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{\text{SISO}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mtext>SISO</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{\text{SISO}}</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e.,</p>
<table id="S2.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\small s_{n}=\sum_{m=0}^{N-1}x_{m}\varphi_{n}(m),n=0,1,\ldots,N-1," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">s</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">n</mi></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em" rspace="0.111em">=</mo><munderover><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em" movablelimits="false" stretchy="true">∑</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">m</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">−</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn></mrow></munderover><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">x</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">m</mi></msub><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">φ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">n</mi></msub><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">m</mi><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">n</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">0</mn><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em" mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">−</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\small s_{n}=\sum_{m=0}^{N-1}x_{m}\varphi_{n}(m),n=0,1,\ldots,N-1,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varphi_{n}(m)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>φ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi_{n}(m)</annotation></semantics></math> is the AFT kernel at the <math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>th SC and associated to the <math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>th modulated symbol. The AFT kernel of Type-A in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">AFDMTWCBemani</span>]</cite> is considered, i.e., <math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varphi_{n}(m)={1\over\sqrt{N}}e^{j2\pi(c_{1}n^{2}+c_{2}m^{2}+{nm\over N})}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>φ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mi>N</mi></msqrt></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mi>N</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi_{n}(m)={1\over\sqrt{N}}e^{j2\pi(c_{1}n^{2}+c_{2}m^{2}+{nm\over N})},</annotation></semantics></math>
where <math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{1}\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{1}\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{2}\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{2}\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math> are the AFDM parameters. Note that (<a href="#S2.E1" title="In II-A1 AFDM modulation ‣ II-A SISO-AFDM Communication Model ‣ II MIMO-AFDM Communication Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>) can be written in the matrix form as
<math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{s}=\Lambda_{c_{1}}^{\mathcal{H}}\mathbf{F}^{\mathcal{H}}\Lambda_{c_{2}}^{\mathcal{H}}\mathbf{x}_{\text{SISO}}\equiv\mathbf{A}^{\mathcal{H}}\mathbf{x}_{\text{SISO}}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐬</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐅</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mtext>SISO</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>≡</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐀</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mtext>SISO</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{s}=\Lambda_{c_{1}}^{\mathcal{H}}\mathbf{F}^{\mathcal{H}}\Lambda_{c_{2}}^{\mathcal{H}}\mathbf{x}_{\text{SISO}}\equiv\mathbf{A}^{\mathcal{H}}\mathbf{x}_{\text{SISO}},</annotation></semantics></math>
where <math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{A}\equiv\Lambda_{c_{2}}\mathbf{F}\Lambda_{c_{1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐀</mi><mo>≡</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐅</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{A}\equiv\Lambda_{c_{2}}\mathbf{F}\Lambda_{c_{1}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the DAFT matrix, <math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Lambda_{c}=\text{diag}\left(e^{-j2\pi cn^{2}},n=0,1,\ldots,N-1\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>diag</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Lambda_{c}=\text{diag}\left(e^{-j2\pi cn^{2}},n=0,1,\ldots,N-1\right)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐅</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{F}</annotation></semantics></math> is the DFT matrix with its element at the <math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>th column and the <math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>th row given by <math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m15" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="e^{-j2\pi mn/N}/\sqrt{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>e</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>j</mi><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msup><mo>/</mo><msqrt><mi>N</mi></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{-j2\pi mn/N}/\sqrt{N}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S2.F1" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2503.19143v1/SISOAFDM.svg" id="S2.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:381/167;" width="381" height="167"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S2.F1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Fig. 1</span>: </span><span id="S2.F1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> Example of SISO-AFDM communication model.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Then, a chirp-periodic prefix (CPP) is applied to the transmitted signal <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">AFDMTWCBemani</span>]</cite>. The CCP with length <math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\text{CPP}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mtext>CPP</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\text{CPP}}</annotation></semantics></math> is given by</p>
<table id="S2.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\small s_{n}=s_{N+n}e^{-j2\pi c_{1}(N^{2}+2Nn)},n=-N_{\text{CPP}},\cdots,-1." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">s</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">n</mi></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">s</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">+</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">n</mi></mrow></msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">e</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">−</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">j</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">c</mi><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi><mn mathsize="0.900em">2</mn></msup><mo mathsize="0.900em">+</mo><mrow><mn mathsize="0.900em">2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">n</mi></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">n</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em" rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.900em">−</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mtext mathsize="0.900em">CPP</mtext></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.900em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo mathsize="0.900em" rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.900em">−</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.900em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\small s_{n}=s_{N+n}e^{-j2\pi c_{1}(N^{2}+2Nn)},n=-N_{\text{CPP}},\cdots,-1.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection"><span id="S2.SS1.SSS2.6" class="ltx_text">II-A</span>2 </span>Channel</h4>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We consider a doubly selective channel with the channel response at time <math id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> and delay <math id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> given by</p>
<table id="S2.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\small g_{n,d}=\sum_{p=1}^{P}h_{p}e^{-j\frac{2\pi}{N}\nu_{p}n}\delta(d-d_{p})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">g</mi><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">n</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">d</mi></mrow></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em" rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em" movablelimits="false" stretchy="true">∑</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">p</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn></mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">P</mi></munderover><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">h</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi mathsize="0.900em">e</mi><mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">−</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">j</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn mathsize="0.900em">2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">π</mi></mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">ν</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">n</mi></mrow></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">d</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">−</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">d</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">p</mi></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\small g_{n,d}=\sum_{p=1}^{P}h_{p}e^{-j\frac{2\pi}{N}\nu_{p}n}\delta(d-d_{p}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the Dirac delta function, <math id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of paths, and <math id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> are the channel gain, Doppler shift and the integer delay of the <math id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>th path, respectively. Note that <math id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> is normalized with respect to the SC spacing and can be expressed as <math id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu_{p}=\alpha_{p}+\beta_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu_{p}=\alpha_{p}+\beta_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{p}\in[-\alpha_{\max},\alpha_{\max}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>max</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>max</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{p}\in[-\alpha_{\max},\alpha_{\max}]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1.m12" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\beta_{p}\in(-\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{p}\in(-\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}]</annotation></semantics></math> denote the integer and fractional parts of <math id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively, and <math id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{\max}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{\max}</annotation></semantics></math> is the maximum integer Doppler.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection"><span id="S2.SS1.SSS3.6" class="ltx_text">II-A</span>3 </span>AFDM demodulation</h4>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The received signal in the time domain after discarding the CPP can be expressed as</p>
<table id="S2.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\small\widetilde{r}_{n}=\sum_{d=0}^{\infty}s_{n-d}g_{n,d}+\widetilde{w}_{n}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">r</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">~</mo></mover><mi mathsize="0.900em">n</mi></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em" rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><munderover><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em" movablelimits="false" stretchy="true">∑</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">d</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">0</mn></mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em" mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></munderover><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">s</mi><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">n</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">−</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">d</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">g</mi><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">n</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">d</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">+</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">w</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">~</mo></mover><mi mathsize="0.900em">n</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\small\widetilde{r}_{n}=\sum_{d=0}^{\infty}s_{n-d}g_{n,d}+\widetilde{w}_{n},</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS1.SSS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{n}\sim\mathcal{CN}(0,N_{0})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{n}\sim\mathcal{CN}(0,N_{0})</annotation></semantics></math> is the additive Gaussian noise. After discarding the CPP, (<a href="#S2.E4" title="In II-A3 AFDM demodulation ‣ II-A SISO-AFDM Communication Model ‣ II MIMO-AFDM Communication Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>) can be re-written in the matrix form as
<math id="S2.SS1.SSS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{\mathbf{r}}=\sum_{p=1}^{P}{\widetilde{{\mathbf{H}}}_{p}}\mathbf{s}+\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐫</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">~</mo></mover><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>P</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐇</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">~</mo></mover><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐬</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐰</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">~</mo></mover></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{\mathbf{r}}=\sum_{p=1}^{P}{\widetilde{{\mathbf{H}}}_{p}}\mathbf{s}+\widetilde{\mathbf{w}},</annotation></semantics></math>
where <math id="S2.SS1.SSS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐰</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the noise vector in the time domain, <math id="S2.SS1.SSS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\widetilde{{\mathbf{H}}}_{p}}=h_{p}\mathbf{\Gamma}_{\text{CPP}_{p}}\mathbf{\Delta}_{\nu_{p}}\mathbf{\Pi}^{d_{p}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐇</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">~</mo></mover><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝚪</mi><msub><mtext>CPP</mtext><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝚫</mi><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝚷</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\widetilde{{\mathbf{H}}}_{p}}=h_{p}\mathbf{\Gamma}_{\text{CPP}_{p}}\mathbf{\Delta}_{\nu_{p}}\mathbf{\Pi}^{d_{p}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the time domain channel matrix of the <math id="S2.SS1.SSS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>th path, <math id="S2.SS1.SSS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\nu_{p}}=\text{diag}(e^{-j\frac{2\pi}{N}\nu_{p}},n=0,1,\ldots,N-1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi <math id="S2.SS1.SSS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{\Pi}={\left[{\begin{array}[]{ cccc}0&amp;\cdots&amp;0&amp;1\\

\vdots&amp;\ddots&amp;\ddots&amp;\vdots\\
0&amp;\cdots&amp;1&amp;0\end{array}}\right]_{N\times N}}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the forward cyclic-shift matrix, and
<math id="S2.SS1.SSS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbf{\Gamma}_{\text{CPP}_{p}}=\text{diag}\left(\left\{\begin{matrix}e^{-j2\pi c_{1}(N^{2}-2N(d_{p}-n))},&amp;n&lt;d_{p},\\
1,&amp;n\geq d_{p},\end{matrix}\right.\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝚪</mi><msub><mtext>CPP</mtext><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><mo>=</mo><mtext>diag</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{\Gamma}_{\text{CPP}_{p}}=\text{diag}\left(\left\{\begin{matrix}e^{-j2\pi c_{1}(N^{2}-2N(d_{p}-n))},&amp;n&lt;d_{p},\\
1,&amp;n\geq d_{p},\end{matrix}\right.\right)</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the effective CCP matrix.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.SSS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, the received signal in the DAFT domain is obtained by applying the DAFT transform, i.e.,</p>
<table id="S2.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\small\mathbf{r}=\Lambda_{c_{2}}\mathbf{F}\Lambda_{c_{1}}\mathbf{\widetilde{r}}\equiv\mathbf{A}\mathbf{\widetilde{r}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐫</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em" mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">c</mi><mn mathsize="0.900em">2</mn></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐅</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em" mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">c</mi><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">𝐫</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">~</mo></mover></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">≡</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐀</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">𝐫</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">~</mo></mover></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.900em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\small\mathbf{r}=\Lambda_{c_{2}}\mathbf{F}\Lambda_{c_{1}}\mathbf{\widetilde{r}}\equiv\mathbf{A}\mathbf{\widetilde{r}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection"><span id="S2.SS1.SSS4.6" class="ltx_text">II-A</span>4 </span>The I/O relation</h4>

lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">𝚲</mi><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">c</mi><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">2</mn></msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">H</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">𝐇</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi mathsize="0.900em">p</mi></msub></munder><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐱</mi><mtext mathsize="0.900em">SISO</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">+</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐰</mi><mtext mathsize="0.900em">SISO</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\sum\limits_{p=1}^{P}{{h_{p}}}\underbrace{{{\mathbf{\Lambda}}_{{c_{2}}}}{\mathbf{F}}{{\mathbf{\Lambda}}_{{c_{1}}}}{{\mathbf{\Gamma}}_{{\mathbf{CP}}{{\mathbf{P}}_{p}}}}{{\mathbf{\Delta}}_{{f_{p}}}}{{\mathbf{\Pi}}^{{d_{p}}}}{\mathbf{\Lambda}}_{{c_{1}}}^{H}{{\mathbf{F}}^{H}}{\mathbf{\Lambda}}_{{c_{2}}}^{H}}_{\overline{{\mathbf{H}}}_{p}}{\mathbf{x}_{\text{SISO}}}+{\mathbf{w}_{\text{SISO}}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="2" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equationgroup ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.E8Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle={{\mathbf{H}_{\text{SISO}}}}{\mathbf{x}_{\text{SISO}}}+{\mathbf{w}_{\text{SISO}}}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐇</mi><mtext mathsize="0.900em">SISO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐱</mi><mtext mathsize="0.900em">SISO</mtext></msub></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">+</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐰</mi><mtext mathsize="0.900em">SISO</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle={{\mathbf{H}_{\text{SISO}}}}{\mathbf{x}_{\text{SISO}}}+{\mathbf{w}_{\text{SISO}}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS4.p1.5" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS1.SSS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{H}_{\text{SISO}}}=\sum\nolimits_{p=1}^{P}{{h_{p}}}{\overline{{\mathbf{H}}}_{p}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>SISO</mtext></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>P</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐇</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{H}_{\text{SISO}}}=\sum\nolimits_{p=1}^{P}{{h_{p}}}{\overline{{\mathbf{H}}}_{p}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the effective channel matrix and <math id="S2.SS1.SSS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{w}_{\text{SISO}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐰</mi><mtext>SISO</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{w}_{\text{SISO}}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the noise vector with the same distribution of <math id="S2.SS1.SSS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐰</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}}</annotation></semantics></math>. It can be shown that the element of <math id="S2.SS1.SSS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\overline{{\mathbf{H}}}_{p}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐇</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\overline{{\mathbf{H}}}_{p}}</annotation></semantics></math> at the <math id="S2.SS1.SSS4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>th row and the <math id="S2.SS1.SSS4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>th column is</p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In AFDM systems, the parameters <math id="S2.SS1.SSS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SS1.SSS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> can be adjusted so that the non-zero elements of matrix <math id="S2.SS1.SSS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\overline{{\mathbf{H}}}_{p}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐇</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\overline{{\mathbf{H}}}_{p}}</annotation></semantics></math> in each path do not overlap within <math id="S2.SS1.SSS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{{\mathbf{H}}_{\text{SISO}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>SISO</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{{\mathbf{H}}_{\text{SISO}}}</annotation></semantics></math>, resulting in a comprehensive delay-Doppler channel representation.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S2.SS2.6" class="ltx_text">II-B</span> </span><span id="S2.SS2.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Frameworks of MIMO-AFDM Schemes</span></h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We consider a MIMO system where the transmitter is equipped with <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> transmit antennas (TAs) and the BS is equipped with <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> receive antennas (RAs). Denoted <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}^{(r,t)}\in\mathbb{C}^{N\times N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐇</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℂ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}^{(r,t)}\in\mathbb{C}^{N\times N}</annotation></semantics></math> by the effective channel matrix from the <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>th TA to the <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>th RA. Then the received signal at the <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>th RA can be expressed as</p>
<table id="S2.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\small\mathbf{y}_{r}=\sum_{t=1}^{N_{t}}\mathbf{H}^{(r,t)}\mathbf{x}_{t}+\mathbf{w}_{r}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐲</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">r</mi></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em" rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><munderover><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em" movablelimits="false" stretchy="true">∑</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn></mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></msub></munderover><mrow><msup><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐇</mi><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">r</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐱</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">+</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐰</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">r</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\small\mathbf{y}_{r}=\sum_{t=1}^{N_{t}}\mathbf{H}^{(r,t)}\mathbf{x}_{t}+\mathbf{w}_{r},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{t}\in\mathbb{C}^{N\times 1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℂ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{t}\in\mathbb{C}^{N\times 1}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the transmitted data at the <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>th TA and <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{w}_{r}\in\mathbb{C}^{N\times 1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐰</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℂ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{w}_{r}\in\mathbb{C}^{N\times 1}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the noise vector with <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{CN}(0,N_{0})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{CN}(0,N_{0})</annotation></semantics></math> entries. By staking the received signal of <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> RAs, we have</p>
<table id="S2.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{y}\equiv\left[\mathbf{y}_{1}^{\mathcal{T}},\mathbf{y}_{2}^{\mathcal{T}},\ldots,\mathbf{y}_{N_{r}}^{\mathcal{T}}\right]^{\mathcal{T}}\in\mathbb{C}^{NN_{r}\times 1}" display="inline" alttext="\mathbf{x}\equiv\left[\mathbf{x}_{1}^{\mathcal{T}},\mathbf{x}_{2}^{\mathcal{T}},\ldots,\mathbf{x}_{N_{t}}^{\mathcal{T}}\right]^{\mathcal{T}}\in\mathbb{C}^{NN_{t}\times 1}" display="inline" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation
