1}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{w}\equiv\left[\mathbf{w}_{1}^{\mathcal{T}},\mathbf{w}_{2}^{\mathcal{T}},\ldots,\mathbf{w}_{N_{r}}^{\mathcal{T}}\right]^{\mathcal{T}}\in\mathbb{C}^{NN_{r}\times 1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>≡</mo><msup><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐰</mi><mn>1</mn><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐰</mi><mn>2</mn><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐰</mi><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi></msup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℂ</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{w}\equiv\left[\mathbf{w}_{1}^{\mathcal{T}},\mathbf{w}_{2}^{\mathcal{T}},\ldots,\mathbf{w}_{N_{r}}^{\mathcal{T}}\right]^{\mathcal{T}}\in\mathbb{C}^{NN_{r}\times 1}</annotation></semantics></math>, and</p>
<table id="S2.E12" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="S2.E12X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow></msup></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">∈</mo><msup><mi mathsize="0.900em">ℂ</mi><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">r</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" mathsize="0.900em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.900em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbf{H}\equiv\left[{\begin{matrix}\mathbf{H}^{(1,1)}&amp;\mathbf{H}^{(1,2)}&amp;\cdots&amp;\mathbf{H}^{(1,N_{t})}\\
\mathbf{H}^{(2,1)}&amp;\mathbf{H}^{(2,2)}&amp;\cdots&amp;\mathbf{H}^{(2,N_{t})}\\
\vdots&amp;\vdots&amp;\ddots&amp;\vdots\\
\mathbf{H}^{(N_{r},1)}&amp;\mathbf{H}^{(N_{r},2)}&amp;\cdots&amp;\mathbf{H}^{(N_{r},N_{t})}\end{matrix}}\right]\in\mathbb{C}^{NN_{r}\times NN_{t}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equationgroup ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Considering the relationship between signals transmitted on different TAs and resource utilization strategies, the MIMO-AFDM frameworks can be categorized into the following two scenarios with the signal mode shown in Fig. <a href="#S2.F2" title="Fig. 2 ‣ II-A4 The I/O relation ‣ II-A SISO-AFDM Communication Model ‣ II MIMO-AFDM Communication Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">1) Scenario 1 (Multiplexing): As shown in <a href="#S2.F2" title="Fig. 2 ‣ II-A4 The I/O relation ‣ II-A SISO-AFDM Communication Model ‣ II MIMO-AFDM Communication Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>(a), the coded bits are split into <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> streams. the <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>th stream is then modulated before transmission over the <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>th antenna.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">2) Scenario 2 (Diversity): As shown in <a href="#S2.F2" title="Fig. 2 ‣ II-A4 The I/O relation ‣ II-A SISO-AFDM Communication Model ‣ II MIMO-AFDM Communication Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>(b), the coded bits are directly modulated with an AFDM modulator. All the <math id="S2.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> TAs transmit the same modulated signal for diversity enhancement.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">III </span><span id="S3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Variational Inference and Graphical Model</span></h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we first present the VI framework <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">Advancesvi</span>]</cite> and the proposed JSG representation in MIMO-AFDM. Then, we detail the message propagation process over the JSG based on VI principles.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S3.SS1.6" class="ltx_text">III-A</span> </span><span id="S3.SS1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Variational Inference</span></h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Given the received observation <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐲</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{y}</annotation></semantics></math>, the goal is to
infer the transmitted signal <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math>. The optimum detection is MAP, which is given by</p>
<table id="S3.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\small\hat{\mathbf{x}}=\mathop{\mathrm{\arg\!\max}}_{{x_{m}\in{\mathcal{X},\forall m}}}\hskip 9.24994ptp({\mathbf{x}}\,|\,{\mathbf{y}})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">𝐱</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">^</mo></mover><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">arg</mi><mo lspace="0.017em">⁡</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">max</mi></mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">x</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">m</mi></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em">∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathsize="0.900em">𝒳</mi></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em" rspace="0.167em">∀</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">m</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐱</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" mathsize="0.900em" rspace="0.170em">|</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐲</mi><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\small\hat{\mathbf{x}}=\mathop{\mathrm{\arg\!\max}}_{{x_{m}\in{\mathcal{X},\forall m}}}\hskip 9.24994ptp({\mathbf{x}}\,|\,{\mathbf{y}}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the constellation alphabet. Solving (<a href="#S3.E13" title="In III-A Variational Inference ‣ III Variational Inference and Graphical Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>) requires a computational complexity order of <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\mathcal{X}|^{NN_{t}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\mathcal{X}|^{NN_{t}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\mathcal{X}|^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mi>N</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\mathcal{X}|^{N}</annotation></semantics></math> for Scenarios 1 and 2, respectively, which increases exponentially with <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. The joint probability of the transmitted vector <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math> and received signal <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐲</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{y}</annotation></semantics></math> can be expressed as: <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\left({\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}}\right)=p\left({\mathbf{x}}\right)p\left({\mathbf{y}|\mathbf{x}}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\left({\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}}\right)=p\left({\mathbf{x}}\right)p\left({\mathbf{y}|\mathbf{x}}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\left({\mathbf{x}}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\left({\mathbf{x}}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the prior probability of <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\left({\mathbf{y}|\mathbf{x}}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\left({\mathbf{y}|\mathbf{x}}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> is the likelihood probability. From Bayes’ rule, the <span id="S3.SS1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">a posterior</span> probability of <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math> is  given by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">Advancesvi</span>]</cite></p>
<table id="S3.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\left({\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{y}}\right)=\frac{p\left({\mathbf{x}}\right)p\left({\mathbf{y}|\mathbf{x}}\right)}{p\left({\mathbf{y}}\right)}\propto p\left({\mathbf{x}}\right)p\left({\mathbf{y}|\mathbf{x}}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>∝</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\left({\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{y}}\right)=\frac{p\left({\mathbf{x}}\right)p\left({\mathbf{y}|\mathbf{x}}\right)}{p\left({\mathbf{y}}\right)}\propto p\left({\mathbf{x}}\right)p\left({\mathbf{y}|\mathbf{x}}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">The marginal posterior probability is calculated as <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\left({{x}_{m}|\mathbf{y}}\right)=\sum_{\sim{x}_{m}}p\left({\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{y}}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\left({{x}_{m}|\mathbf{y}}\right)=\sum_{\sim{x}_{m}}p\left({\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{y}}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> which serves as the soft information output for the channel decoder, where <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{\sim{x}_{m}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{\sim{x}_{m}}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the summation over all the arguments except <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{m}</annotation></semantics></math>. Unfortunately, the direct calculation of <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\left({{x}_{m}|\mathbf{y}}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\left({{x}_{m}|\mathbf{y}}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> incurs high computational complexity. As an approximation approach, the VI technique can be employed for efficient compute (<a href="#S3.E14" title="In III-A Variational Inference ‣ III Variational Inference and Graphical Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a>). The  core idea  of VI is to find a distribution <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q(\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{y})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q(\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{y})</annotation></semantics></math> from a tractable distribution family <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math>, serving as an optimized approximation of the target posterior distribution <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{y})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{y})</annotation></semantics></math>. As such, the inference problem in (<a href="#S3.E14" title="In III-A Variational Inference ‣ III Variational Inference and Graphical Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a>) can be transformed to a tractable optimization problem.
The widely used optimization metrics in VI are the exclusive Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{KL}(p|q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>KL</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{KL}(p|q)</annotation></semantics></math> and inclusive KL divergence <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{KL}(q|p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>KL</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{KL}(q|p)</annotation></semantics></math>, which measure the similarity between two distributions. The <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{KL}(p|q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>KL</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{KL}(p|q)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{KL}(q|p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>KL</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{KL}(q|p)</annotation></semantics></math> are respectively defined as <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">Advancesvi</span>]</cite></p>
<table id="S3.E15" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="S3.E15X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E15X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\text{KL}(q|p)=" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext mathsize="0.900em">KL</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">q</mi><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.900em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">p</mi><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\text{KL}(q|p)=</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E15X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\sum_{\mathbf{x}}q\left({\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{y}}\right)\log\frac{q\left({\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{y}}\right)}{p\left({\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{y}}\right)}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em" movablelimits="false" stretchy="true">∑</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐱</mi></munder></mstyle><mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐱</mi><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.900em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐲</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐱</mi><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.900em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐲</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐱</mi><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.900em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐲</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\sum_{\mathbf{x}}q\left({\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{y}}\right)\log\frac{q\left({\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{y}}\right)}{p\left({\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{y}}\right)},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="2" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equationgroup ltx_align_right">(15)</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.E15Xa" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E15Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\text{KL}(p|q)=" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext mathsize="0.900em">KL</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">p</mi><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.900em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">q</mi><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\text{KL}(p|q)=</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Note that the KL divergence is non-negative.
Moreover, it is neither symmetric nor a distance metric, i.e., <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{KL}(p|q)\neq\text{KL}(q|p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext>KL</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mtext>KL</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{KL}(p|q)\neq\text{KL}(q|p)</annotation></semantics></math>. <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{KL}(q|p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>KL</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{KL}(q|p)</annotation></semantics></math> divergence emphasizes assignment of low probability mass of <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> to the location where <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> is very small. In other words, <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{KL}(q|p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>KL</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{KL}(q|p)</annotation></semantics></math> has the propriety of “mode-seeking” or “zero-forcing” as it forces <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> to concentrate on one of the local maximum values of <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>. Conversely, <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{KL}(p|q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>KL</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{KL}(p|q)</annotation></semantics></math> divergence emphasizes assignment of high probability mass of <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> to the location where <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> has positive mass. Namely, <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{KL}(p|q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>KL</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{KL}(p|q)</annotation></semantics></math> metric has the property of mean-seeking or mass covering, meaning that <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> tends to fit the mean value of <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In a nutshell, the VI framework provides a unified structure to design detection algorithms by taking <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{KL}(q|p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>KL</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{KL}(q|p)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{KL}(p|q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>KL</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{KL}(p|q)</annotation></semantics></math> into consideration. In addition, the VI framework can also be described by using a powerful probabilistic graphical model known as a factor graph. This graphical representation is the key for low-complexity algorithm design, which will be discussed in the sequel.</p>
</div>

</figure></div></div>

</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S3.SS2.6" class="ltx_text">III-B</span> </span><span id="S3.SS2.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Joint Factor Representation in MIMO-AFDM</span></h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recall (<a href="#S2.E9" title="In II-A4 The I/O relation ‣ II-A SISO-AFDM Communication Model ‣ II MIMO-AFDM Communication Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>), for each path, <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta(d_{p},n,m)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta(d_{p},n,m)</annotation></semantics></math> has unit energy, and one has <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">AFDMTWCBemani</span>]</cite></p>
<table id="S3.E16" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="S3.E16X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E16X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\left|{\overline{\mathbf{H}}_{p}}[n,m]\right|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">𝐇</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi mathsize="0.900em">p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">[</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">n</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">m</mi></mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\left|{\overline{\mathbf{H}}_{p}}[n,m]\right|</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E16X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\left|\frac{1}{N}\gamma(d_{p},\nu_{p},n,m)\right|=\left|\frac{\sin{(N\theta)}}{N\sin{(\theta)}}\right|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">γ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">d</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">p</mi></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">ν</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">p</mi></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">n</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">m</mi><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">sin</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi></mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">sin</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\left|\frac{1}{N}\gamma(d_{p},\nu_{p},n,m)\right|=\left|\frac{\sin{(N\theta)}}{N\sin{(\theta)}}\right|</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E16Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\underset{\leq}{(\text{i})}\frac{N-1}{N}\left|{{\cos(\theta)}}\right|+\frac{1}{N}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><mtext mathsize="0.900em">i</mtext><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow><mo mathsize="0.630em">≤</mo></munder><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">−</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn></mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">+</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\underset{\leq}{(\text{i})}\frac{N-1}{N}\left|{{\cos(\theta)}}\right|+\frac{1}{N},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta\triangleq\frac{\pi}{N}(n-m+\mathrm{Ind}_{p}+\beta_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>Ind</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta\triangleq\frac{\pi}{N}(n-m+\mathrm{Ind}_{p}+\beta_{p})</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\overline{\mathbf{H}}_{p}}[n,m]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐇</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\overline{\mathbf{H}}_{p}}[n,m]</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the entry at the <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>th row and <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>th column of <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\overline{\mathbf{H}}_{p}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐇</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\overline{\mathbf{H}}_{p}}</annotation></semantics></math>,
and the detailed derivation of <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\text{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext>i</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\text{i})</annotation></semantics></math> is given by the Equations (35) and (36) of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">AFDMTWCBemani</span>]</cite>. The above bounds hold tight as <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> increases. It is noted that
<math id="S3.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma(d_{p},\nu_{p},n,m)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma(d_{p},\nu_{p},n,m)</annotation></semantics></math> achieves the peak energy at <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m=(n+\text{Ind}_{p})_{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mtext>Ind</mtext><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>N</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m=(n+\text{Ind}_{p})_{N}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the elements in <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\overline{\mathbf{H}}_{p}}[n,m]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐇</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\overline{\mathbf{H}}_{p}}[n,m]</annotation></semantics></math>
become insignificant as <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> moves away from <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(n+\text{Ind}_{p})_{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mtext>Ind</mtext><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>N</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(n+\text{Ind}_{p})_{N}</annotation></semantics></math>.
To better present the message passing over the VI graph, we first assume that those insignificant elements in <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\overline{\mathbf{H}}_{p}}[n,m]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐇</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\overline{\mathbf{H}}_{p}}[n,m]</annotation></semantics></math> are zeros when <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> falls outside of <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[n+\text{Ind}_{p}-\nu_{v},n+\text{Ind}_{p}+\nu_{v}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mtext>Ind</mtext><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mtext>Ind</mtext><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[n+\text{Ind}_{p}-\nu_{v},n+\text{Ind}_{p}+\nu_{v}]</annotation></semantics></math>. Namely,</p>

<p id="S3.SS2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">In Subsection <a href="#S4.SS2" title="IV-B Sparse Channel Based on eSNR ‣ IV The proposed E-JSG ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">IV-B</span></a>, we will present the proposed sparse channel scheme to address these insignificant elements and determine <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{\nu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>ν</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{\nu}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">A factor graph is a bipartite graph representing the factorization of a joint distribution function <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐱</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐲</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})</annotation></semantics></math>. Fig. <a href="#S3.F3" title="Fig. 3 ‣ III-A Variational Inference ‣ III Variational Inference and Graphical Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>(a) shows an example of <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\overline{\mathbf{H}}_{p}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐇</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\overline{\mathbf{H}}_{p}}</annotation></semantics></math> in a SISO-AFDM system with <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">N</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=16</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{\nu}=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">k</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">ν</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{\nu}=2</annotation></semantics></math>. Consider the one-path channel in Fig. <a href="#S3.F3" title="Fig. 3 ‣ III-A Variational Inference ‣ III Variational Inference and Graphical Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>(a), the factor graph is shown in Fig. <a href="#S3.F3" title="Fig. 3 ‣ III-A Variational Inference ‣ III Variational Inference and Graphical Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>(b). Each AFDM variable node (AVN) is connected to <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2k_{\nu}+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">k</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">ν</mi></msub></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">+</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2k_{\nu}+1</annotation></semantics></math> function nodes (FNs) and each FN is also occupied by <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2k_{\nu}+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">k</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">ν</mi></msub></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">+</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2k_{\nu}+1</annotation></semantics></math> AVNs. For simplicity, denote <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{m}^{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{m}^{t}</annotation></semantics></math> as the transmitted symbol at the <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>th SC of the <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>th TA. Consider the MIMO-AFDM of Scenario <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>, the joint distribution <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐱</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐲</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})</annotation></semantics></math> can be factorized as</span></p>

<p id="S3.SS2.p2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">where <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" id="S3.SS2.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{n,m}^{r,t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">h</mi><mrow><mi encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>th SC of the <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>th TA to the <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>th SC of the <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>th RA, and <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(x_{m}^{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(x_{m}^{t})</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the prior probability of <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{m}^{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{m}^{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. The factor graph can be designed to contain <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="NN_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">N</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">NN_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> AVNs <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{m}^{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{m}^{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{r}N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">N</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{r}N</annotation></semantics></math> likelihood FNs <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{n}^{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">f</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{n}^{r}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The LDPC codes can also be represented by a bipartite graph called Tanner graph with the belief messages passing over the LDPC VNs (LVNs) and LDPC check nodes (CNs). In this paper, we propose to design the JSG-based receiver by merging the VI factor graph and the LDPC graph into an integrated one. As a result, the belief messages are exchanged iteratively on a JSG. Fig. <a href="#S3.F4" title="Fig. 4 ‣ III-B Joint Factor Representation in MIMO-AFDM ‣ III Variational Inference and Graphical Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> shows an example of the JSG for the MIMO-AFDM of Scenario <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>. The AVNs and FNs represent the transmit layers and the likelihood function <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(y^{r}_{n}|\mathbf{x})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi></msubsup><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐱</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(y^{r}_{n}|\mathbf{x})</annotation></semantics></math>.
The set of AVN indices sharing the <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>th FN of the <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>th RA is denoted as <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F(n,r)=\left\{{(m,t):h_{n,m}^{r,t}\neq 0}\right\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">{</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">h</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi></mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">≠</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(n,r)=\left\{{(m,t):h_{n,m}^{r,t}\neq 0}\right\}</annotation></semantics></math>, whereas the set of FN indices sharing the <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>th VN is denoted by <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m30" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="V(m,t)=\left\{{n,r:h_{n,m}^{r,t}\neq 0}\right\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">V</mi><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">{</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0.278em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">h</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi></mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">≠</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V(m,t)=\left\{{n,r:h_{n,m}^{r,t}\neq 0}\right\}</annotation></semantics></math>. In addition, the cardinalities of <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V(m,t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">V</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V(m,t)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F(n,r)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(n,r)</annotation></semantics></math> are denoted as <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|V(m,t)|=d_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">V</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">d</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">f</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|V(m,t)|=d_{f}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|F(n,r)|=d_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">d</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">v</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|F(n,r)|=d_{v}</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively.
In this paper, we first consider the MIMO-AFDM in Scenario <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>, and the results can be readily extended to Scenario <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m36" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>

<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S3.SS3.6" class="ltx_text">III-C</span> </span><span id="S3.SS3.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">BP-JSG</span></h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">In this subsection, we first consider the optimization metric as the exclusive KL divergence, i.e., </span><math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{KL}(p|q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">KL</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{KL}(p|q)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS3.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">. It is well known that the </span><math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS3.p1.2.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> partition function </span><math id="S3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log p({\mathbf{y}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐲</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log p({\mathbf{y}})</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS3.p1.2.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> can be decomposed as </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><span id="S3.SS3.p1.2.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">[</span><span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">Factorbp</span><span id="S3.SS3.p1.2.6" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">]</span></cite></p>

<p id="S3.SS3.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">where </span><math id="S3.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathscr{L_{\mathrm{ELBO}}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathscript" mathcolor="#000000">ℒ</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">ELBO</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathscr{L_{\mathrm{ELBO}}}}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS3.p1.3.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> is the evidence lower bound (ELBO). Namely, </span><math id="S3.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathscr{L_{\mathrm{ELBO}}}}=\log p({\mathbf{y}})-\text{KL}(q|p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathscript" mathcolor="#000000">ℒ</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">ELBO</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐲</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">−</mo><mrow><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">KL</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathscr{L_{\mathrm{ELBO}}}}=\log p({\mathbf{y}})-\text{KL}(q|p)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS3.p1.3.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">. As a result, instead of minimizing </span><math id="S3.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{KL}(p|q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">KL</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{KL}(p|q)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS3.p1.3.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, one can maximize </span><math id="S3.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathscr{L_{\mathrm{ELBO}}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathscript" mathcolor="#000000">ℒ</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">ELBO</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathscr{L_{\mathrm{ELBO}}}}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS3.p1.3.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">. To solve this problem, we resort to the Bethe approximation for maximizing </span><math id="S3.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathscr{L_{\mathrm{ELBO}}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathscript" mathcolor="#000000">ℒ</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">ELBO</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathscr{L_{\mathrm{ELBO}}}}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS3.p1.3.6" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">. It is shown that the stationary points of the Bethe approximation to the </span><math id="S3.SS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathscr{L_{\mathrm{ELBO}}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathscript" mathcolor="#000000">ℒ</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">ELBO</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathscr{L_{\mathrm{ELBO}}}}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS3.p1.3.7" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> are equivalent to the fixed points of the standard BP algorithm </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><span id="S3.SS3.p1.3.8" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">[</span><span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">Factorbp</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">VIchen</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">meng2015expectation</span><span id="S3.SS3.p1.3.9" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">]</span></cite><span id="S3.SS3.p1.3.10" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">. Denote </span><math id="S3.SS3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{v_{m}^{t}\rightarrow f_{n}^{r}}^{l}({x}_{m}^{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle+\sum_{m,t\in F(n,r)}L_{v_{m}^{t}\rightarrow <p id="S3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The message propagation within the LDPC graph and between the LDPC and VI graph will be discussed along with the proposed EP-JSG.</span></p>
