<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S3.SS4.6" class="ltx_text">III-D</span> </span><span id="S3.SS4.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">EP-JSG</span></h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">In BP-JSG, (</span><a href="#S3.E20" title="In III-C BP-JSG ‣ III Variational Inference and Graphical Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">)-(</span><a href="#S3.E21" title="In III-C BP-JSG ‣ III Variational Inference and Graphical Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">21</span></a><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">) require global searches over the joint space of all symbols, which is a discrete set. Consequently, the computational complexity of BP-JSG is exponential, i.e., </span><math id="S3.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}\left(M^{Pk_{\nu}}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathcolor="#000000">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">(</mo><msup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">M</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">k</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">ν</mi></msub></mrow></msup><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}\left(M^{Pk_{\nu}}\right)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">. As </span><math id="S3.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, </span><math id="S3.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, and </span><math id="S3.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{\nu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">k</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">ν</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{\nu}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> increase, BP-JSG becomes impractical in real-world systems, especially in scenarios with high mobility and rich scattering environments as </span><math id="S3.SS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> and </span><math id="S3.SS4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{\nu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">k</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">ν</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{\nu}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> typically have large values. Instead of using </span><math id="S3.SS4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{KL}(q|p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">KL</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{KL}(q|p)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, we resort to the inclusive </span><math id="S3.SS4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{KL}(p|q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">KL</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{KL}(p|q)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.11" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> as the optimization metric. The objective is to find a distribution family </span><math id="S3.SS4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q(\mathbf{x})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐱</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q(\mathbf{x})</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.12" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> that minimizes </span><math id="S3.SS4.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{KL}(p|q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">KL</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{KL}(p|q)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.13" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">. Although global optimization is intractable, it can be iteratively solved using the well-known EP algorithm </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.14" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">[</span><span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">EPT</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">VIchen</span>, <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">meng2015expectation</span><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.15" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">]</span></cite><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.16" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">. Denote </span><math id="S3.SS4.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{v_{m}^{t}\rightarrow f_{n}^{r}}^{l}({x}_{m}^{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mrow><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">v</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi></msubsup><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">→</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">f</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi></msubsup></mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">l</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi></msubsup><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{v_{m}^{t}\rightarrow f_{n}^{r}}^{l}({x}_{m}^{t})</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.17" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> and </span><math id="S3.SS4.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{f_{n}^{r}\rightarrow v_{m}^{t}}^{l}({x}_{m}^{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mrow><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">f</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi></msubsup><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">→</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">v</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi></msubsup></mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">l</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi v_{m}^{t}}^{l}({x}_{m}^{t})</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.18" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> as the belief messages propagated from VN </span><math id="S3.SS4.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{m}^{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">v</mi><mi alttext="f_{n}^{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">f</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathsize="0.900em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\small q_{n,{r}}^{t}({x}_{m}^{t})\propto\sum_{{x}_{m\prime}^{t\prime}\neq{x}_{m}^{t}}p(y_{n}^{r}|{x}_{m\prime}^{t\prime})\prod_{m\prime,t\prime\in F(n,r)\backslash\{m,t\}}I_{v_{m}^{t}\rightarrow f_{n}^{r}}^{t}({x}_{m}^{t}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(25)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The above procedure can be understood as the messages propagation over the VI graph depicted in Fig. </span><a href="#S3.F4" title="Fig. 4 ‣ III-B Joint Factor Representation in MIMO-AFDM ‣ III Variational Inference and Graphical Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a><span id="S3.SS4.p1.3.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.
It treats the messages exchanged between VNs and FNs as continuous random variables and approximates the true distribution with a Gaussian distribution, characterized by its mean and variance. This approach enables signal detection to be transformed into the computation of mean and variance, avoiding the need to traverse all symbols. Specifically, we have</span></p>

m,t}^{l},\xi_{n,r\rightarrow m,t}^{t}}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(26c)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.p1.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Now, we introduce the detailed message propagation in the proposed JSG.</span></p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS4.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection"><span id="S3.SS4.SSS1.6" class="ltx_text">III-D</span>1 </span>Updating of VNs</h4>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">In the separate graph case, VNs only gather information from one type of nodes (FNs or CNs). However, in the JSG, the updating of VNs in JSG involves the information from both sub-graphs. Let </span><math id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{\alpha_{i}\rightarrow\beta_{j}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" <p id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p2.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Then, based on (</span><a href="#S3.E28" title="In III-D1 Updating of VNs ‣ III-D EP-JSG ‣ III Variational Inference and Graphical Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">28</span></a><span id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p2.4.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">), the </span><span id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p2.4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">a posterior</span><span id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p2.4.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> belief probability for AVN </span><math id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{m}^{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{m}^{t}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p2.4.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> can be calculated as</span></p>

<p id="S3.SS4.SSS2.p1.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.SSS2.p1.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">where </span><math id="S3.SS4.SSS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{sign}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">sign</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{sign}(x)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS4.SSS2.p1.4.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> denotes the the sign of </span><math id="S3.SS4.SSS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS4.SSS2.p1.4.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.</span></p>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.SSS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">On the FN side, the calculation of </span><math id="S3.SS4.SSS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{n,r\rightarrow m,t}^{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">μ</mi><mrow><mi The received signal </span><math id="S3.SS4.SSS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{n}^{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{n}^{r}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS4.SSS2.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> is considered as the sum of transmitted signals from all layers plus the noise. <section id="S3.SS4.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection"><span id="S3.SS4.SSS3.6" class="ltx_text">III-D</span>3 </span>Extrinsic and prior LLRs exchange</h4>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.SSS3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The output extrinsic information of the VI detector are utilized as the </span><span id="S3.SS4.SSS3.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">a priori</span><span id="S3.SS4.SSS3.p1.2.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> LLRs for the LDPC decoder. <p id="S3.SS4.SSS3.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.SSS3.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Denote </span><math id="S3.SS4.SSS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" <p id="S3.SS4.SSS3.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.SSS3.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">At the LVN side, it gathers information from CNs by</span></p>

<p id="S3.SS4.SSS3.p2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.SSS3.p2.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">where </span><math id="S3.SS4.SSS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS4.SSS3.p2.5.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">th bit of </span><math id="S3.SS4.SSS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathcolor="#000000">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.SS4.SSS3.p2.5.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.SSS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.SSS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Remark 1: The proposed JSG allows belief messages from the LDPC
and VI graphs to propagate in a joint manner. In addition, the
AVNs (FNs) and LVNs (CNs) are able to update messages
simultaneously, leading to faster convergence with fewer iterations.
</span></p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">IV </span><span id="S4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">The proposed E-JSG</span></h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Note that messages in the VI graph are updated at the symbol level, whereas messages in the LDPC graph are updated on a per-bit basis. This mismatch between symbol-level message updates in the VI graph and bit-level updates in the LDPC graph results in inefficient message propagation. Furthermore, the computation of bit-to-symbol and symbol-to-bit LLRs introduces higher computational complexity.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">To address these challenges, we propose an E-JSG, which enables message updating on a per-bit basis. Moreover, to further reduce computational complexity, we introduce a sparse channel method based on the eSNR,  which helps eliminate unnecessary message propagation over the E-JSG.</span></p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F5" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2503.19143v1/FactorGraph_EJSG.svg" id="S4.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_portrait" style="aspect-ratio:310/427;" width="310" height="427"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F5.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Fig. 5</span>: </span><span id="S4.F5.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> Factor representation of the proposed E-JSG.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S4.SS1.6" class="ltx_text">IV-A</span> </span><span id="S4.SS1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The Proposed E-JSG</span></h3>

<section id="S4.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection"><span id="S4.SS1.SSS1.6" class="ltx_text">IV-A</span>1 </span>Linear encoding-inspired VI graph design</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Let us consider the linear encoding for a modulation process in the following way </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><span id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">[</span><span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">SCMAE2E2</span><span id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.2.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">]</span></cite></p>
<table id="S4.E44" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E44.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{x}=\mathbf{g}\mathbf{u}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐠𝐮</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{x}=\mathbf{g}\mathbf{u},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(44)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">where </span><math id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mrow><msup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐇</mi><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">t</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐆</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\mathbf{H}}^{(r,t)}=\mathbf{H}^{(r,t)}\mathbf{G}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.5.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> denotes the combined channel matrix. By utilizing (</span><a href="#S4.E46" title="In IV-A1 Linear encoding-inspired VI graph design ‣ IV-A The Proposed E-JSG ‣ IV The proposed E-JSG ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">46</span></a><span id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.5.6" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">), the VI graph designed only contains bit VNs (BVNs) instead of the symbol VN. Hereafter, the VNs in the E-JSG are referred to as the BVNs. As a result, the LLR calculation for bit to symbol is no longer required and the interleaver (deinterleaver) can also be eliminated. Fig. </span><a href="#S4.F5" title="Fig. 5 ‣ IV The proposed E-JSG ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a><span id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.5.7" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> shows an example of a folded view of the proposed E-JSG, where </span><math id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">M</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=4</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.5.8" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> is considered. Based on the JSG framework introduced in Section </span><a href="#S3" title="III Variational Inference and Graphical Model ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">III</span></a><span id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.5.9" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, both FNs and CNs are able to update their messages concurrently. Subsequently, the BVNs of VI and LDPC subgraphs simultaneously update the mean and variance, and LLR to FNs and CNs, respectively. Therefore, it is reasonable to place FNs (rectangles) and CNs (triangles) on one side, while drawing BVNs (circles) on the other side. Note that one circle contains </span><math id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log_{2}M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">log</mi><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log_{2}M</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.5.10" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> BVNs.</span></p>
</div>

<p id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">In this paper, we consider </span><math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">M</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=4</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.4.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> with </span><math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{g}=[1,-1j]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐠</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">−</mo><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">j</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{g}=[1,-1j]</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.4.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">. n,r}^{l}\left({\frac{\mu_{i}^{l}}{\xi_{i}^{l}}-\frac{\mu_{n,r\rightarrow i}^{l-1}}{\xi_{n,r\rightarrow i}^{l-1}}}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection"><span id="S4.SS1.SSS3.6" class="ltx_text">IV-A</span>3 </span>Update of CNs and FNs to BVNs</h4>

mathsize="0.900em">i</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em" rspace="0.1389em">′</mo><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0.1389em" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em" stretchy="false">→</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">n</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">r</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">l</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">−</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">1</mn></mrow></msup><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i\prime\in\overline{F}(n,r),\\
i\prime\neq i\end{subarray}}|\overline{h}^{i\prime}_{n,r}|^{2}\xi_{i\prime\rightarrow n,r}^{l-1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.SSS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS3.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.SSS3.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Finally, the posterior probabilities of the transmitted symbol in LLR domain is given by</span></p>

<p id="S4.SS1.SSS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.SSS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The overall message propagation of the proposed E-JSG is summarized in Algorithm (</span><a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ IV-A1 Linear encoding-inspired VI graph design ‣ IV-A The Proposed E-JSG ‣ IV The proposed E-JSG ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a><span id="S4.SS1.SSS3.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">).</span></p>

</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S4.SS2.6" class="ltx_text">IV-B</span> </span><span id="S4.SS2.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sparse Channel Based on eSNR </span></h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">In the proposed JSG and E-JSG, the computational complexity depends crucially on the degree at each FN, which is determined by </span><math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> and </span><math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{\nu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">κ</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">ν</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{\nu}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">. Specifically, the degree at each FN of E-JSG is upper bounded by </span><math id="S4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P\kappa_{\nu}\log_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">κ</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">ν</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">log</mi><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">2</mn></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">M</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P\kappa_{\nu}\log_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.  In general, </span><math id="S4.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> and </span><math id="S4.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{\nu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">κ</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">ν</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{\nu}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> tend to be relatively large, particularly in rich scattering scenarios and when fractional Doppler shift is significant. To reduce the computational complexity of the JSG and E-JSG, one possible approach is to reduce the number of edges of the VI graph,  i.e., select a small value of </span><math id="S4.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{\nu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">κ</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">ν</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{\nu}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> for each </span><math id="S4.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\overline{\mathbf{H}}_{p}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐇</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\overline{\mathbf{H}}_{p}}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, thereby reducing unnecessary message propagation. This is reasonable as some of the non-zero elements in </span><math id="S4.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{H}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝐇</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{H}}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> has very small amplitude, the message propagating over the corresponding edges may not significantly improve the error rate performance.  To this end, we propose a sparse channel method based on eSNR to determine the nonzero elements for message passing, which is equivalent to determine </span><math id="S4.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{\nu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">k</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">ν</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{\nu}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, and to approximate multiple graph edges with
insignificant channel coefficients as a single edge on the VI
graph.</span></p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F6" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2503.19143v1/H_C.svg" id="S4.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:262/264;" width="262" height="264"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F6.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Fig. 6</span>: </span><span id="S4.F6.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> An example
of the selected entries, highlighted by the red lines, for message propagation of a two-path channel. </span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Denote the set of non-zero channel coefficients at the FN </span><math id="S4.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{n}^{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">f</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{n}^{r}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p2.2.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> as </span><math id="S4.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}(n,r)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathcolor="#000000">𝒟</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}(n,r)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p2.2.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, and let </span><math id="S4.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D=|\mathcal{D}(n,r)|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">D</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathcolor="#000000">𝒟</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D=|\mathcal{D}(n,r)|</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p2.2.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> return the cardinalities of </span><math id="S4.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}(n,r)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathcolor="#000000">𝒟</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}(n,r)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p2.2.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">. Then, we sort the </span><math id="S4.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p2.2.6" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> non-zero channel coefficients in descending
order and choose the </span><math id="S4.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\text{L}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">D</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">L</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\text{L}}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p2.2.7" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> largest terms, denoted as </span><math id="S4.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\text{L}}(n,r)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">D</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">L</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\text{L}}(n,r)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p2.2.8" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, for message propagation over the VI graph. We further denote </span><math id="S4.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\text{S}}(n,r)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">D</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">S</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\text{S}}(n,r)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p2.2.9" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> as the remaining terms. Then, the edges corresponding to the </span><math id="S4.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\text{S}}(n,r)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">D</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">S</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\text{S}}(n,r)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p2.2.10" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> are approximated as a single edge. Consequently, the means and variance in (</span><a href="#S4.E51" title="In IV-A3 Update of CNs and FNs to BVNs ‣ IV-A The Proposed E-JSG ‣ IV The proposed E-JSG ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">51</span></a><span id="S4.SS2.p2.2.11" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">) and (</span><a href="#S4.E52" title="In IV-A3 Update of CNs and FNs to BVNs ‣ IV-A The Proposed E-JSG ‣ IV The proposed E-JSG ‣ Joint Sparse Graph for Enhanced MIMO-AFDM Receiver Design" class="ltx_ref" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">52</span></a><span id="S4.SS2.p2.2.12" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">) are computed respectively as follows</span></p>

<div id="S4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">By approximating the insignificant edges as a single edge, it allows more efficient message passing. encoding="application/x-tex">G_{s}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}|{\mathbf{H}}^{(r,t)}[n,(n\prime+s)_{N}]|^{2}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.22" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">. The elements at the </span><math id="S4.SS2.p3.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.23" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">th cyclic-shift is added into </span><math id="S4.SS2.p3.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\text{L}}(n,r)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">D</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">L</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">r</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\text{L}}(n,r)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.24" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> for message propagation if and only if the eSNR of the </span><math id="S4.SS2.p3.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.25" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">th cyclic-shift is larger than a threshold, i.e,</span></p>
<table id="S4.E55" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E55.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\small\text{eSNR}_{s}\equiv 10\log\frac{G_{s}}{N_{0}}\geq\text{eSNR}_{\text{th}},0\leq s\leq N-1," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">eSNR</mtext><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathsize="0.900em">0</mn></msub></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.900em">≥</mo><msub><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" <p id="S4.SS2.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">where </span><math id="S4.SS2.p3.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{eSNR}_{\text{th}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">eSNR</mtext><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">th</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{eSNR}_{\text{th}}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p3.2.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> denotes the threshold, and </span><math id="S4.SS2.p3.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{eSNR}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">eSNR</mtext><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{eSNR}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p3.2.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> denotes the eSNR at the </span><math id="S4.SS2.p3.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS2.p3.2.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">th cyclic-shift.       should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
